message.content:
Lions mate during a brief but intense courtship period that typically lasts only a few days. Male lions form coalitions—groups of related males that defend a pride together—and they compete for dominance within the coalition. When a male or coalition approaches a pride, they will engage in a ritualized display that includes roaring, scent marking, and physical posturing. If the female (lioness) is receptive, she will allow the male(s) to mount her. 

During copulation, the male mounts the female from behind, and the two may remain in this position for several minutes. After mating, the male may stay with the female for a short time to guard her against rival males. Once the female gives birth, the male’s role is largely protective; he defends the pride’s territory and helps guard the cubs from other males. This mating strategy ensures that the strongest males have the best chance of passing on their genes while also protecting the offspring from infanticide.
